title: Reliability, Availability, Maintainability & System Performance

canonicalTerminology.definition: Reliability is the ability of an item to perform a required function under stated conditions for a stated period or usage context.

claims.text: RAMS thinking examines reliability, availability, maintainability and safety as interacting lifecycle properties rather than isolated metrics.
claims.applicabilityNote: Level-neutral educational statement; adapt depth without changing the canonical fact.

equations.limitation: Basic teaching relationship; real RAM models require precise state definitions, censoring rules and data treatment.

visualSpecs.purpose: Show RAMS lifecycle interactions and feedback.

prohibitedUnsupportedClaims: Do not invent reliability targets, SIL-like thresholds or acceptance criteria.
Do not present simplified RAM calculations as validated safety evidence.
